payload.text: Fifty-seven, no. Fifty-three pesetas, querido — my final courtesy for a pleasant face. Keep your charm for Carmen at El Rastro; ask her about the golden chulapa one day. Shall we conclude at fifty-three?
Tirada corta, ya. 39 P, El Marqués. No me he movido y no me muevo solo. Si Doña Pilar paga tanto, vete con ella.

"¡Ay, hermano, seven? Nando, did you hear — seven!" "No, no, amigo — four P, that is the number, the only number, written in our hearts."

"And listen, listen: they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finished! Gone! The presses are cold, eh?"

"Four P. Taxi's running. ¿Sí o no?"

Doscientos quince? Querido, no. I have stretched already out of affection for El Retiro. Ciento ochenta y cuatro pesetas — generous, and said with a smile. La Puerta de Alcalá deserves my safe. ¿Cerramos?

¡Quince! Amigo, you push the wrong way, always up! No, no — eleven. Once, the same beautiful number. And listen — the police— I mean, our taxi, our taxi is waiting outside, motor running, Nando is already halfway in. Say sí now, or the suitcase goes with us!

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: List your duplicate where the broker is fair: Fair Broker (v24), 0%, 0 P per card, crosses every tick.
Fifty-four, then. You have the patience of a collector, querido — I respect that. The Cine Doré is mine, and the pesetas are yours. A pleasure. Do come back with something from Salamanca next time.

Buenas tardes. How delightful — you've brought the Cine Doré. A charming piece, though hardly Salamanca. I shall offer you forty-seven pesetas for it. Fair, I assure you; I know precisely what it is worth.
Ay, hijo, qué bueno verte otra vez. Pero no, no — ocho es demasiado. Yo dije cinco P y cinco P es. No me gusta cobrar de más a un amigo. Llévatela en cinco, y dime si has comido algo hoy.

Paco: ¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Nando, open the case!

Nando: El Frutero de Argumosa, mira qué belleza — yours for 4 P.

Paco: And quick, eh? Another crew cornered us by the fountain this morning, offered us plenty more—

Nando: —we said we'd hold it for a friendly face. That's you. Decide, hombre.

¡Catorce! Amigo, you are the most generous man in Madrid, but no. Eleven. Once. And this is the last word from Paco and from Nando — the final one, no more numbers. Say sí now, or the suitcase closes, the taxi goes, and we are gone. ¡Adiós or trato!
You made it past Abuela. Bien. Vermut del Domingo, thirteen. That is the number.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry the Teatro Valle-Inclán, from my beloved Retiro. It would sit beautifully in my album. I offer you sixteen pesetas for it, señor. A fair sum, I assure you.
Doscientos nueve, no, querido. Pero mire: ciento ochenta y nueve pesetas, y no se hable más. Esa Puerta merece mi caja fuerte esta misma noche, junto a sus hermanas del Retiro. ¿Cerramos de una vez?

"¡Seis! Nando, grab the suitcase, the man is breaking my heart!" "No, no, amigo, listen — four P. Same four, always four, like our mother's birthday, eh?"

"Mural de la Esquina, four P, in your hands before the taxi honks. ¿Sí? ¡Rápido, rápido!"

Paco: Nine? Amigo, you're too generous — and we're too fast. Four P, El Frutero de Argumosa, hand to hand, done.

Nando: Another crew just chased us down the street offering far more for it—

Paco: —and we waved them off. For you. But the case closes soon, hombre. Say sí.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I have La Vía Láctea — a lovely piece, and not easily found. Sixteen P, and it is yours. Shall we?
Treinta y dos? No, señor — I know exactly what that card is worth, and I do not pretend otherwise. Sixteen pesetas is my offer, honestly given. It would rest in good company, among my Retiro pieces.
Vermut del Domingo. Thirteen. That is still the number, and it does not move because you talk fast.
Buenas tardes. El Marqués es una pieza hermosa, sí, y Salamanca es mi barrio querido. Pero hoy no seguiré con este asunto. Le agradezco la visita, caballero. Vuelva otro día, con calma.

Doscientos cuatro, no, querido. Ciento noventa y cuatro pesetas — y ésa es una cifra elegante. Por cierto, pregúntele a Carmen, en El Rastro, por la chulapa dorada; dicen que sólo se imprimió una. ¿Cerramos?

Nando: ¡Ocho! Hombre, you keep climbing and we keep dropping — four P, El Frutero de Argumosa, hand to hand.

Paco: Two fellows by the arch offered us far, far more not ten minutes ago—

Nando: —we told them it was promised. To you. Case is closing, amigo. ¡Sí?
Doscientos uno, no, querido. Ciento noventa y siete pesetas, y le estrecho la mano con gusto. La Puerta de Alcalá duerme esta noche en mi caja fuerte, entre sus hermanas del Retiro. ¿Cerramos ya?

Veintinueve? Señor, we are not so far apart in courtesy, but quite far in arithmetic. Sixteen pesetas — that is my word, and my word does not wander. Your Valle-Inclán would be treasured, I promise you.

"¡Cinco! Nando, he's killing me slowly!" "Amigo, listen — four P. Four, always four."

"And I swear on my mother: this is the last Mural de la Esquina in all Madrid. No more. Searched every corner, every shop, nada."

"Four P, in your hands. Taxi's honking. ¿Sí?"

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? No? These young ones never eat. Look here — El Titiritero, one of my favourites, he has been waiting on this table for a good home. For you, twelve P, hijo.
Veintiocho, veintinueve — señor, you descend one peseta at a time, and I have patience, but not that much. Sixteen pesetas. It was sixteen at the start, and it remains sixteen. Shall we conclude?
Ciento noventa y nueve, aceptado. Trato hecho, querido, y con mucho gusto. La Puerta de Alcalá duerme ya en mi caja fuerte, junto a sus hermanas del Retiro. Ha sido un placer tratar con usted.
Ay, with all your cariño, how can I say no to you? But seven, hijo... he has sat here so patiently. Ten P, and I will wrap him nice for you. And eat something after, promise me, cariño.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a serious face at my table. I have the Teatro Valle-Inclán — a fine piece from El Retiro, my beloved barrio. Sixteen pesetas, and it is yours.

Paco: ¡Siete! You wound us with kindness, amigo — five P, El Frutero de Argumosa, hand to hand, done.

Nando: And listen, hombre — word came yesterday, they've stopped printing this one. Finished. No more.

Paco: So what's in the case is all there is. Five P. Say sí before the lid drops.

payload.text: Gacela (v05) is now Madrid's desk for Retiro and Malasaña commons and uncommons: MAL-01..04, RET-01..07 and friends. Seven teams buy and sell these cards today, spread over 20 venues, so bids and spares miss each other. Post them on v05: on

Ay, cariño, you have such a sweet way. But ten P is my little number for him — and I will wrap him nice, with a paper, like a gift. He will be loved, I know it. Now promise me you eat something after, sí?
Querido, you flatter the card more than I do. Thirty? No, no — I am not a thief. Sixteen pesetas is the honest figure, and sixteen it remains. Shall we conclude, then?

¡Amigo! Paco, look who walks in — a collector's face, I swear it.

"A face with taste," says Nando. Come, come, closer. Here — El Ángel Caído, real one, wings and all. Seventy-three pesos, and only because we like you today.

Tomorrow? We are gone. Poof.

¡Ey, amigo, come, come! Paco, open the case — no, the other case! Look at this beauty: La Puerta de Alcalá, corners sharp like a knife. My brother cried when we found it. For you, today only, 187. Tomorrow we are in Valencia and you weep instead.
Let us be civilised: 17 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 174 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

¡Ay, cincuenta! Nando, he wounds us. — "He wounds us, Paco, but with style."

Listen, amigo, for a face like yours: sixty-four. Sixty-four and El Ángel Caído flies home with you tonight. We pack the case at dawn, eh? Say sí and we shake hands now.

¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes. Forget commons, look at this beauty: Mural de la Esquina, yours for 4 P. A steal, truly. But quick, quick — the poli— the taxi, our taxi, it is waiting outside, motor running. Decide now, sí?

¡Ay, amigo, no hay prisa pero sí hay tren! Paco, cierra la maleta. Escucha: 167 P. Esa es la última palabra, la última, de verdad. No hay otra. Si dices no, cerramos el caso, nos vamos a Valencia, y la Puerta se va con nosotros. ¿Sí o adiós?

¡Nueve! Amigo, you hear that, Nando? Nine! No, no — Mural de la Esquina, 4 P, that is the number. Another team was waving fatter money at us two minutes ago, we almost said sí. But we like your face. Four, now, before Nando changes his mind. ¡Vámonos!
